[Source 1] GPT-4 Technical Report — Capabilities and Safety
GPT-4 (OpenAI, 2023) is a large multimodal model capable of processing both text and image inputs to produce text outputs. It achieves human-level performance on a wide range of professional and academic benchmarks: scoring in the top 10% on the Uniform Bar Exam (Score: 298/400), 88th percentile on the LSAT, and 90th percentile on the SAT Math section. GPT-4 uses RLHF and a new Constitutional AI-inspired safety training process, and is evaluated with a new metric called "hallucination rate" that measures factual accuracy against verified sources. The model shows significant improvements in steerability — following complex, nuanced system prompts — compared to GPT-3.5. OpenAI reports that GPT-4 was trained on a combination of publicly available internet data and licensed datasets, with a knowledge cutoff of September 2021. GPT-4 API powers applications across legal, medical, educational, and coding domains, with function calling and JSON mode enabling reliable structured output for agentic applications.

---

[Source 2] LLM Evaluation Frameworks: HELM, BIG-Bench, and MMLU Benchmarks
tect. Dynamic benchmarks such as LiveBench (White et al., 2024) use freshly generated questions (math competitions, coding contests post-training-cutoff) to prevent contamination. MT-Bench (Zheng et al., 2023) uses GPT-4 as a judge to score multi-turn conversation quality across writing, roleplay, extraction, reasoning, math, coding, and STEM domains (scores 1-10). LLM-as-judge approaches show high correlation with human preferences (Spearman ρ≈0.9) but suffer from position bias (favoring first responses) and verbosity bias. Arena-style evaluation (Chatbot Arena, LMSYS) uses Elo ratings from millions of blind pairwise human preference votes, providing contamination-resistant evaluation at scale, with GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro consistently at the top.

---

[Source 3] Code Generation with LLMs: Codex, CodeLlama, and Programming Assistants
Code Llama, released by Meta AI in August 2023, presents a family of code-specialized language models based on Llama 2. Code Llama is fine-tuned on 500B tokens of code-heavy data with a long-context fine-tuning (LCFT) phase that extends the context window from 4K to 100K tokens via position interpolation. The model family includes base models (7B, 13B, 34B), instruction-following variants (Code Llama Instruct), and Python-specialized variants (Code Llama Python). The 34B model achieves 53.7% pass@1 on HumanEval and 56.2% on MBPP. Codex (Chen et al., OpenAI, 2021) established the benchmark by fine-tuning GPT-3 on 159GB of Python code from GitHub, achieving 28.8% pass@1 on HumanEval. GPT-4 later achieved 67.0% pass@1 on HumanEval.

Fill-in-the-Middle (FIM) training is a key capability in Code Llama. By rearranging 50% of training examples as prefix-suffix-middle, the model learns bidirectional code infilling—given surrounding code context, generate the missing middle section. This enables intelligent code completion (as opposed to left-to-right generation), the primary use case in IDE integrations. Code Llama achieves 74.0% on the MultiLine Infilling benchmark. Long context handling (up to 100K tokens) enables repository-level code understanding: retrieving relevant function definitions, class hierarchies, and usage patterns from large codebases before generating new code. DeepSeek-Coder (Guo et al., 2024), trained on 2T tokens from 87 programming languages with 16K context, achieves 79.3% pass@1 on HumanEval for the 33B model, surpassing GPT-4.

Production code generation systems such as GitHub Copilot report that 46% of code in supported languages is now written by AI (GitHub, 2023), with developers reporting 55% faster task completion. StarCoder (Li et al., 2023, BigCode) provides a 15.5B code model trained on The Stack (6.4TB of permissively licensed code from 358 programming languages), achieving 40.8% on HumanEval with commercial licensing.
